nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
(اسم) is in the genitive (makhfūḍ) through the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: The bāʾ was given kasra to distinguish between what makes a noun genitive while being only a particle and nothing else, and what makes a noun genitive while it may sometimes be a noun, such as the kāf. It may be asked: why did the bāʾ come to make nouns genitive? The answer to this, and for all the genitive-governing particles, is that these particles have no meaning except in nouns, and they do not resemble verbs so as to govern as verbs govern; so they were given what occurs only in nouns, namely the genitive (khafḍ) — the early Basrans call it jarr. The position of the bāʾ and what follows it is, according to al-Farrāʾ, accusative, in the sense of "I began with «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم»" or "I begin with «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم»"; according to the Basrans it is nominative, in the sense of "my beginning is with the name of Allah". ʿAlī ibn Ḥamza al-Kisāʾī said:
The bāʾ has no grammatical position, and the "passing" falls upon something unspecified when you say: مررت بزيد ("I passed by Zayd").
The alif in «اسم» is a connecting alif (alif waṣl), because you say سُمَيّ (in the diminutive); for this reason it is dropped in pronunciation. As for its being dropped in writing, there are four views: al-Farrāʾ said it is because of frequent use; it is also reported [that it was dropped] because the bāʾ is never written separately; al-Akhfash Saʿīd said it was dropped because it is not part of the pronunciation; and the fourth view is that the original form is سِم and سُم. Abū Zayd recited: [al-Rajaz metre]
1-
بسم الذي في كلّ سورة سمه
(In the name of the One whose name is in every sura.)
— also with ḍamma, so that the original would be سما; then you brought the bāʾ and it became بسم, then the kasra was dropped and it became بسم. On this view there was never an alif in it at all. [Translator's note: the text as printed reads «ثم حذفت الكسرة فصار بسم» ("then the kasra was dropped and it became بسم"); the vowelling needed to follow the argument (presumably بِسِم → بِسْم) has been lost in the source.] The original pattern of اسم is fiʿl; it can only be that, for a reason that requires it. Its plural is أسماء, and the plural of أسماء is أسامي. You made اسم muḍāf (in a genitive construct) to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; the alif in "Allah" is a connecting alif according to those who say the original is لاه. Some of the Arabs make it a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ) and say بسم الله [pronouncing the hamza], because it always accompanies the word, like a disjunctive alif.
«الرَّحْمنِ» is a naʿt (adjective) of Allah the Exalted. It is not put in the dual or plural, because it is used only of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The lām is assimilated into the rāʾ because of their closeness and because the lām of definiteness is so frequent.
«الرَّحِيمِ» is also a naʿt; its plural is رحماء. This [form] is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, Banū Asad, Qays and Rabīʿa; Banū Tamīm say رِحيم, رِغيف, بِعير [with kasra on the first letter]. [Translator's note: the printed text shows these words without vowelling; the Tamīmī kasra on the first letter is the well-known feature intended.] In pausing you may give the kasra a trace (ishmām) or make it quiescent; quiescence is better with what has kasra, and ishmām is more common with what has ḍamma.
The accusative is permissible in «الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ» as praise (madḥ), and the nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is also permissible to make the first genitive and the second nominative, or to make one of them nominative and the other accusative.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
«الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ»: [الحمد] is nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the view of the Basrans. Al-Kisāʾī said: «الحمد» is nominative through the pronoun that is in the "ṣifa", the ṣifa being the lām — he treated the lām like a verb. Al-Farrāʾ said:
«الحمد» is nominative through the "maḥall", which is the lām — he treated the lām like a noun, because it cannot stand by itself. Al-Kisāʾī calls the genitive-governing particles ṣifāt ("qualifiers"), al-Farrāʾ calls them maḥāll ("places"), and the Basrans call them ẓurūf ("adverbials/containers"). Ibn ʿUyayna and Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj read «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. in the accusative, الحمدَ لله], and this is the dialect of Qays and al-Ḥārith ibn Sāma. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling «الْحَمْدُ» here although it describes the accusative reading; likewise in the variant readings below, the printed Quranic text does not show the variant vowels being described.] The nominative is better both in wording and in meaning. As for wording: because it is a definite noun about which you have predicated. As for meaning: if you use the nominative you are stating that your praise and the praise of others belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; if you use the accusative, it does not go beyond your own praise. Al-Farrāʾ reported: «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» and «الحمد لله» [i.e. الحمدِ لِلّه and الحمدُ لُلّه].
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the Younger] say: neither of these two is permissible according to the Basrans. Abū Jaʿfar said: These are two known dialects and two existing readings, and each has a rationale. Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related from Zurayq from al-Ḥasan that he read «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» [i.e. الحمدِ لِلّه], and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla read «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» [i.e. الحمدُ لُلّه]; this is the dialect of some of Banū Rabīʿa, and the kasra is the dialect of Tamīm. As for the dialect with kasra: this phrase is very frequent in people's speech, and ḍamma is heavy, especially when a kasra follows it; so they replaced the ḍamma with kasra and treated the two as a single thing — kasra with kasra is lighter, and likewise ḍamma with ḍamma; that is why «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» was said [in these two ways].
«لِلَّهِ» is genitive through the lām, which is zāʾida (redundant). [Translator's note: the source says «باللام الزائدة»; the lām here is not normally classed as redundant, but it is translated as written.] Sībawayh held that the original vowel of the lām is fatḥa; what shows you this is that when you use a pronoun you say الحمد لَهُ, returning it to its origin; it was given kasra only with an overt noun, to distinguish between the lām of the genitive and the lām of emphasis (tawkīd).
«رَبِّ» is genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of Allah. «الْعالَمِينَ» is genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct); the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, because it is of the same kind as kasra. The nūn, according to Sībawayh, is as it were a compensation for the vowel and the tanwīn that were withheld; according to Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] the nūn is a compensation for the tanwīn; and according to Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] a compensation for the vowel. It was given fatḥa to distinguish it from the nūn of the dual. Al-Kisāʾī said: «رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ» is permissible [in the accusative, ربَّ العالمين], as you say:
الحمد لله ربًّا وإلهًا ("praise be to Allah as Lord and God"), i.e. as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Ḥātim said: the accusative is in the sense of "I praise Allah, the Lord of the worlds". Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative is permissible as a vocative (nidāʾ) in construct. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: the accusative as a vocative in construct is far-fetched, because it would make it two separate utterances; rather it is accusative as praise (madḥ). The nominative is also permissible, i.e. "He is the Lord of the worlds". Abū Jaʿfar said: We mentioned in the earlier book that, for intensiveness, one says ربّاه, ربّه and ربّته. Its explanation is that the original is ربّبه, then a yāʾ is substituted for the bāʾ, as one says:
قصّيت أظفاري and تقصّيت [from قصّصت, "I clipped my nails"], then a tāʾ is substituted for the yāʾ, just as it is substituted for the wāw in تالله.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t:
«الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ» is permissible [in the accusative] as praise (madḥ); it is permissible to make both nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is permissible to make one of them nominative and the other accusative; and it is permissible to make the first genitive and the second nominative or accusative.
Muḥammad ibn al-Samayfaʿ al-Yamānī read «مالك يوم الدّين» with مالك in the accusative. There are four dialectal forms of it: مالِك, مَلِك, مَلْك and مَلِيك, as Labīd said: [al-Kāmil metre] 2-
فاقنع بما قسم المليك فإنّما ... قسم المعايش بيننا علّامها
(Be content with what the Sovereign has apportioned, for the One who apportioned livelihoods among us is the One who knows them best.)
In terms of Arabic [grammar] there are twenty-five ways [of reading] it: one says «ملك يوم الدين» as a naʿt (adjective); in the nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ; in the accusative as praise, as a vocative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and as a naʿt according to the reading of those who read «رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ» [in the accusative]. These are six ways; «مالك» has the same, «مَلْك» has the same, and «مليك» has the same. That makes twenty-four. The twenty-fifth is reported from Abū Ḥaywa Shurayḥ ibn Yazīd, that he read «ملك يوم الدّين», and it is also reported from him that he read «ملك يوم الدين». [Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes these two reported readings is missing from the source; in other works Abū Ḥaywa is credited with the verbal reading مَلَكَ يومَ الدين.] Abū Jaʿfar said: the plural of مالك is مُلّاك and مُلَّك; the plural of مَلِك is أملاك and ملوك; and the plural of مَلْك is أَمْلُك and ملوك — this on the view of those who say «مَلْك» is a dialectal form and not a quiescent-ised form of مَلِك. The plural of مليك is مُلَكاء.
«يَوْمِ» is genitive by مالك being put in construct with it, and «الدِّينِ» is genitive by يوم being put in construct with it. The plural of يوم is أيّام; the original is أَيْوام: the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ. No verb is used from it.
Sībawayh held that if a verb were used from it, one would say يُمْتُ. The plural of الدين is أديان and ديون.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
«إِيَّاكَ» is accusative because «نَعْبُدُ» falls upon it [as its object]. Al-Faḍl ibn ʿĪsā al-Raqāshī read «إِيَّاكَ» with fatḥa on the hamza [أَيّاك], and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «إِيَّاكَ» without shadda [إِياك]. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard form in both cases; the variants are as described in the words.] The noun in إيّاك, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is إيّا, and the kāf is in the position of the genitive; according to the Kufans, إيّاك in its entirety is the noun. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, held that it is a pronoun noun. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: this is a mistake — a pronoun is not put in construct; rather it is a vague noun (mubham) like «كلّ», put in construct with what follows it.
«نَعْبُدُ» is an imperfect verb (fiʿl mustaqbal); it is nominative according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh because of its resemblance to nouns. Al-Kisāʾī said: the imperfect verb is nominative through the added letters at its beginning. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is nominative through its being free from the jussive- and subjunctive-governing particles.
The [second] «إِيَّاكَ» is accusative through «نستعين» — a clause conjoined to a clause. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read «نَسْتَعِينُ» with kasra on the nūn [نِستعين], and this is the dialect of Tamīm, Asad, Qays and Rabīʿa. They did this to show that it is from استعون يستعين. The original of «نستعين» is نستعوِن: the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the ʿayn, and when what precedes the wāw had kasra it became a yāʾ. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is استعانة, the original being استعوان: the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the ʿayn, and when what precedes the wāw had fatḥa it became an alif. Two quiescent letters cannot meet, so the second alif was dropped because it is the augment — and it is said [rather] the first, because the second carries a meaning — and the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] was made obligatory as a compensation.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
«إِنَّا هُدْنا» [Translator's note: so printed in the source; the word under discussion is clearly «اهْدِنَا» of verse 6, and the heading appears to be a transcription error.] — it is a supplication and a request; according to al-Farrāʾ it is in the position of the jussive (jazm), and according to the Basrans it is in a state of pause (waqf) [i.e. indeclinable], and for that reason the yāʾ was dropped. The alif is a connecting alif (alif waṣl), because the first letter of the imperfect has fatḥa; you gave it kasra because it is from يهدي. The nūn and alif are the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «الصِّراطَ» is the second object. Its plural of paucity is أَصْرِطة and its plural of abundance is صُرُط. Al-Akhfash said: the people of the Hijaz treat الصراط as feminine. Ibn ʿAbbās read «السراط» with sīn, and some of Qays pronounce it between ṣād and zāy; it is not permissible to make it a [pure] zāy unless it is quiescent. Quṭrub said: if, after the sīn within the same word, there is a ṭāʾ, a qāf, a khāʾ or a ghayn, you may change it into a ṣād.
«الْمُسْتَقِيمَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of الصراط.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
«صِراطَ الَّذِينَ»: [صراط] is a badal (substitute). «الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct); it is indeclinable (mabnī) so that a noun is not declined from its middle. «أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ» is part of the ṣila (relative clause), and the hāʾ and mīm refer back to الذين. In «عليهم» there are five dialectal forms, all of which have been read. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «أنعمت عليهُمُو» with ḍamma on the hāʾ and the wāw retained; this is the original, that the wāw be retained just as the alif is retained in the dual. Al-Ḥasan read «أنعمت عليهِمِي» with kasra on the hāʾ and the yāʾ retained: he gave the hāʾ kasra because he disliked combining a yāʾ and a ḍamma, the hāʾ being no strong barrier, and he substituted yāʾ for the wāw because what preceded it had kasra. The people of Medina read «عَلَيْهِمْ» with kasra on the hāʾ and the mīm quiescent; this is the dialect of the people of Najd. Ḥamza and the people of Kufa read «عَلَيْهُمْ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ and the mīm quiescent; they dropped the wāw because of its heaviness, and because the meaning is not ambiguous since in the dual one says عليهما. The fifth form was read by al-Aʿraj: «عليهِمُو» with kasra on the hāʾ and [ḍamma before] the wāw. [Translator's note: the source says «بكسر الهاء والواو», literally "with kasra of the hāʾ and the wāw"; translated as written, with the intended form supplied in brackets.] Two anomalous forms are also reported: ḍamma on both the hāʾ and the mīm without wāw, and kasra on both without yāʾ. [Translator's note: the source reads «لغتنا», evidently for «لغتان», "two dialectal forms".] Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is not permissible, because it is mustaqbal [Translator's note: so in the source; the word seems corrupt — perhaps «مستثقل», "felt to be heavy"]. If it is asked: why then is منهُ said, with ḍamma on the hāʾ? The answer is that the nūn in «منه» is quiescent. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: some people of Banū Bakr ibn Wāʾil say عليكِم, giving the kāf kasra just as they give the hāʾ kasra, because it is a voiceless (mahmūsa) letter like it, and it is a pronoun just as the hāʾ is a pronoun. This is a gross error, because it is not like it in faintness.
«غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ» is genitive as a badal (substitute) from الذين, or, if you wish, as a naʿt (adjective). Ibn Kaysān said: it may also be a badal from the hāʾ and mīm in عليهم. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr «غَيْرَ الْمَغْضُوبِ» in the accusative. Al-Akhfash said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or, if you wish, as an exception (istithnāʾ). Abū al-ʿAbbās said: it is an exception not of the same kind as what precedes (istithnāʾ laysa min al-awwal). The Kufans said: it cannot be an exception, because «ولا» comes after it, and «لا» is not added in exception. Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not follow, because it carries the meaning of negation. He said «غير المغضوب عليهم» and did not say "المغضوبين" because there is no pronoun in it. Ibn Kaysān said: it is singular with a plural meaning, and so is every passive participle when it has no nominative pronoun [Translator's note: the source reads «إذا لم يكن فيه خفض مرفوع», literally "when it has no nominative genitive"; the wording seems disturbed and is rendered by sense], such as المنظور إليهم and المرغوب فيهم. «الْمَغْضُوبِ» [is genitive] by غير being put in construct with it, and «عَلَيْهِمْ» is in the position of the nominative because it is the noun whose agent is not named [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)].
«وَلَا» is zāʾida (redundant) according to the Basrans and in the sense of غير according to the Kufans. «الضَّالِّينَ» is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «المغضوب عليهم»; the Kufans call this nasq, and Sībawayh calls it ishrāk ("association"). The original of الضالّين is الضاللين; then the lām was assimilated into the lām, so two quiescent letters met, and this was allowed because the alif has prolongation and the second is assimilated. However, Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī used a hamza and read «وَلَا الضَّأْلِّينَ».
